content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I set up the screen on the [product_name] operator device to show Flag status when turned on or off. During simulation, everything worked fine, but after transferring the program to the PLC and [product_name] operator device, the Flag status did not display as expected. Can someone assist with this issue? I'm unsure why there's a difference between the simulation and the real display. Regards,
Hi, [user_name]. The F1-F4 keys on the [product_name] operator device act as momentary pushbuttons in actual display operation. To resolve this, you need to add an extra block called 'pulse relay'.

Hello, I think you are using the Status-Text feature. Please verify which [product_name] version you have. Generally, status text functionality has been available since [product_name] [version_no]. New features were added with [product_name] [version_no], while earlier versions only allowed status text for digital inputs and outputs. Status text for flags, cursor keys, function keys, shift register bits, and function block outputs became possible with [product_name] [version_no]. Hope this information helps.

Dear all, thanks for your responses. [user_name], based on your explanation, if I need to display status for function blocks, counters, flags, etc. as text on the display, I have to use [version_no]. Is that correct? I appreciate your clarification.

Hello, if you're using status text then yes, that's correct. For viewing function block parameters within message text, it's possible with [product_name] [version_no] and the operator device, but only up to FB200. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered differences between simulation and actual hardware behavior, specifically regarding flag status display on the [product_name] operator device. The issue stems from version-specific feature support, with older versions lacking full capability. Unclear documentation on which versions support particular status text features has led to confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that the [product_name] operator device display matches simulation performance, especially in showing flag statuses and status texts for various elements during real-time operation.
